context.canonical_title: Java 浅拷贝与深拷贝的区别

required_checks: Verify the candidate directly answers both restored source rows, including aliasing in complex nested structures and the practical testing impact of shared mutable children.
Verify Object.clone() is described as a field-for-field shallow copy and that mutable deep structure is not implied to be recursively cloned.
Verify Cloneable is treated as a marker controlling Object.clone() eligibility, not as a clone method contract or an automatic deep-copy mechanism.
Verify array and collection examples preserve the one-level boundary: multidimensional array clone creates one new outer array with shared subarrays, and ArrayList.clone() does not clone elements.
Verify deep-copy graph traversal preserves cycles and repeated-reference topology by tracking already-processed nodes by reference identity rather than equals().
Verify immutable references may be shared when their semantics are actually immutable, while mutable state that must evolve independently is copied according to explicit business semantics.

Verify Java serialization is presented as a serializable object-graph traversal option with reference sharing, compatibility/custom-serialization cost, and untrusted-deserialization security boundaries rather than a universal low-cost solution.
Verify copy-after-completion isolation is not conflated with obtaining a concurrency-consistent snapshot while the source graph is being mutated.

Verify the concept-answer contract includes a concise definition, shared comparison dimensions, selection conditions, inapplicable boundaries, concrete confusions/counterexamples, and at least three topic-specific answered follow-ups.
review_contract.promotion_boundary: Do not promote or fabricate human approval. This canonical is in the pilot review scope and requires the repository's mandatory human-review attestation after evidence and deterministic audit pass.

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: Object (Java SE 25 & JDK 25): clone()
claims_to_check: Object.clone() initializes fields as if by assignment, does not clone field contents, and therefore performs a shallow copy
independence may require copying mutable objects in the deep structure while immutable references normally need no modification

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: Cloneable (Java SE 25 & JDK 25)
claims_to_check: Cloneable indicates that Object.clone() may make a field-for-field copy
Cloneable contains no clone method and Object.clone() remains protected by default

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: Java Language Specification SE 25, Chapter 10 Arrays
claims_to_check: array clone creates a new array object
a multidimensional array clone is shallow and shares subarrays

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: ArrayList (Java SE 25 & JDK 25): clone()
claims_to_check: ArrayList.clone() returns a shallow copy and does not copy the elements

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: IdentityHashMap (Java SE 25 & JDK 25)
claims_to_check: IdentityHashMap compares keys by reference identity
topology-preserving transformations such as deep-copying use an identity-based node table of already-processed references

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: ObjectOutputStream (Java SE 25 & JDK 25)
claims_to_check: ObjectOutputStream writes graphs of serializable objects transitively
reference sharing is encoded so an object graph can be restored with the same shape

primary_sources_to_verify_independently.title: java.io package (Java SE 25 & JDK 25)
claims_to_check: deserialization of untrusted data is inherently dangerous and should be avoided or strictly validated
